Methods for simple_mconv objects

Source: R/methods.simple_mconv.R
simple_mconv-methods.Rd

Methods defined for objects returned from method_convert().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'simple_mconv'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

# S3 method for class 'simple_mconv'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.simple_mconv'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

# S3 method for class 'simple_mconv'
check(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'simple_mconv'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'simple_mconv'
confint(object, parm = c("all", "alpha", "beta"), level = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'simple_mconv'
predict(object, newdata, from = NULL, to = NULL, level = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'simple_mconv'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("conversion", "ba"),
  pair = NULL,
  geom = c("geom_point", "geom_bin2d", "geom_density_2d", "geom_density_2d_filled",
    "stat_density_2d"),
  delta = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x, object

Object of class simple_mconv, as returned from method_convert().

digits

The number of digits to print.

...

further arguments passed through, see description of return value for details.

parm

Which parameters to include: "all" (default), "alpha" (intercepts), or "beta" (slopes).

level

For confint, the confidence level (default: the conf_level of the fit). For predict, the coverage of the prediction limits (default: the pred_level of the fit).

newdata

Values of the from method on the original scale: a numeric vector, or a data frame with a column named after the from method.

from, to

Names of the methods to convert from and to. Default: from the first method to the second.

type

Type of plot. "conversion" (default): the to method against the from method on the original scale, with the observed pairs, the line of identity (dashed), and the conversion with its prediction limits. "ba": a Bland-Altman plot of the differences (first minus second method of pair) with the bias and prediction limits implied by the model, as lines that change with the level (linear bias or scaled model). For a conversion from a method_vc() fit, the bias is constant and the plot is that of the fit (see simple_mvc-methods): the bias and limits are points with their confidence intervals, to the left of the data.

pair

Character vector of two method names. For type = "conversion", c(from, to); for type = "ba", the difference is first minus second. Default is the first two methods.

geom, delta

For type = "ba", the geometry used to display the data points and the maximal allowable difference; see simple_mvc-methods.

Value

print

Prints the conversion equations (intercept, slope, and prediction SD) with confidence intervals.

coef

Named vector of the conversion parameters, alpha[to|from] and beta[to|from].

confint

Matrix of confidence limits for the conversion parameters: percentile intervals from the bootstrap estimates for ci_method = "boot", otherwise from the standard errors and the t distribution.

predict

A tibble with the values converted from from to to on the original scale: from_value, fit, and the prediction limits lower and upper. Values outside the domain of the transformation give NA.

plot

A ggplot object.

summary

An object of class summary.simple_mconv whose print method shows the fit details (iterations and convergence for the scaled model, bootstrap failures; with estimator = "ml", the log-likelihood, any zero or negative variance estimates, and the model fit: chi-square test, RMSEA and SRMR), the design, the number of pairs used, the regressions of the differences on the averages (linear bias) or the per-method intercepts and slopes (scaled), the conversions, and the variance components.

check

A patchwork of diagnostic plots, as for agreement_limit(), with what to look for in each subtitle and the tests in the captions. Linear bias, for each pair: a normal QQ plot of the standardized residuals of the regression of the differences on the averages (Shapiro-Wilk test); the square root of the absolute standardized residuals against the averages (Breusch-Pagan test; with variance = "linear", the residuals are divided by the fitted SD); and the residuals against the averages (RESET test of linearity). The last two use item means, so replicates are not counted more than once. Scaled model: normal QQ plots of the standardized residuals of the final variance component model by method (Shapiro-Wilk tests), the square root of their absolute values against the fitted true values (Breusch-Pagan tests), and the intercepts and slopes at each iteration of the alternating regression. With estimator = "ml", the residuals are from the factor scores of the true values, item-by-replicate and method-by-item effects, and the iteration panel is replaced by a caption with the convergence and model fit. Not available for conversions from method_vc(); use check() on that fit.
